ENV-01.sheet: A single 3D-model reference turnaround sheet on a plain light-gray studio background: the same floating shelf of dark rock 40 m wide and 56 m long with a ragged asymmetric outline, about 6 m thick at the rim and tapering into an inverted cone 48 m deep with a faint bronze vein glowing inside it, six thick rusted chains hanging from bronze rim rings into the haze. At the near end is the SPAWN TERRACE, an irregular paved patch about 13 x 9 m of cracked slabs of different sizes, with a shallow bronze arrival disc (3.6 m across, three concentric rings, slightly sunken and cracked) at its centre and a low broken rock lip behind it; a tiny plain 1.8 m human silhouette stands on the disc facing the door in every view for scale. A broken road of uneven worn slabs about 4 m wide, with a thin broken bronze inlay line, leads about 11 m to THE BEAM: one colossal weathered bronze I-girder 16 m long with a 2.5 m wide top, lying slightly crooked (about 15 degrees off the straight line) across a ragged meandering crack that cuts the whole island from rim to rim, 8 to 11 m wide with stepped broken lips and a 60 m drop into haze; the beam is level but dented, rust-streaked, matte, dusty, with missing rivets and a chipped corner, never polished. Beyond it a broken irregular forecourt about 13 x 4 m, then three worn uneven steps rising to THE DOOR, shown LOCKED, cut into the face of a huge black rock cliff with raw rock on both sides: 8 m high, carved stone frame 7.6 m wide with a crown of bronze finials, battered green-bronze verdigris scrollwork leaves dark with soot, two thick rusted chains wound across both leaves held by one huge closed padlock, a thin bright amber line of light through the centre gap, exactly like the Core Fantasy key-art door. Behind the door the cliff holds a walkable antechamber: a 3 m passage, then an irregular carved hall about 16 x 11.5 m with an 11 m cracked ceiling, four stout columns (two whole, two broken) around a clear aisle, a low round dais 4.5 m across where three weapons hover, completely dark inside with no daylight (only the faint glow of the weapons), a small west alcove, and, at the east side of the hall, a short flight of 5 wide worn stone steps going DOWN into a 4 m opening (the exit tunnel) in the east wall that leads out onto a rock ledge on the cliffs east face where a fixed bridge leaves toward the next island. The door sits low at the foot of ONE enormous, deep, solid mountain of black-brown fractured rock that rises 36 m at its west shoulder and 60 m at its summit, as thick and heavy as it is tall, with a huge cave carved inside it. The whole mass is built from countless big rough boulders, slabs, ribs and buttresses piled and jammed together, so the area around the door is crowded with many large rocks and ledges, with broken scree at their feet. Its upper part splits into two high crooked peaks (60 m and a 36 m one leaning west), which are simply the top of the same mass, not separate objects. All one rock: NO windows, NO openings, NO bricks or cut stone, NO tiers, NO battlements, NO carvings, nothing built. Only a faint amber glow deep in a few natural cracks. Around the base stand six chunky broken rock outcrops of 20 to 48 m, different heights, thick at the base, blunt snapped tops, NOT needles, NOT cones, NOT icicles. NO masonry on them: no bricks or courses of cut stone, no battlements, no crenellations, no arched windows, no columns, no domes, no bands or carved panels, nothing that looks built, Roman or medieval. Three bare dead trees (6 m, 4.5 m, and a 2.8 m broken stump) stand off the road, a few small uneven clumps of dry grass, and rubble in uneven scatters of different-sized stones; no mirror symmetry anywhere, immense, silent and ominous; match the attached approved ENV-01 hero image and blueprint sheets exactly, and add no second floating island or extra rock in the background, shown from 6 angles in one image, arranged in a clean grid (front, back, left side, right side, top, underside). Every view must be the exact same object with identical design, proportions and scale, rendered with neutral even studio lighting and no shadows hiding detail, no scene, no camera tilt. A large bold title banner at the top reading exactly "ENV-01 - STARTING SHELF ISLAND" with a smaller size note "~40 x 56 m" beside it, and a small label under each view with the angle name; all text short, high-contrast, spelled correctly, each label appears only once. Every island must have a dramatically unique, instantly recognizable grand silhouette with one signature feature, immense sense of scale, mysterious ancient engineered ruins, deep volumetric haze and warm rim light, interesting to look at from every angle. Match the approved key art: weathered sandstone-tan and dark charcoal-brown layered rock with obsidian-black shards, warm gold-amber dusty haze light, photoreal cinematic game-asset concept, rough eroded surfaces with sharp fractured edges, sparse dry dead fossil-like trees and thin dry grass tufts only. REAL, NOT A TOY: photoreal massive geology and ancient ruined architecture, as if photographed at full size. Heavy erosion, soot, dust, deep cracks, spalled and chipped stone, rust and verdigris streaks, irregular asymmetric forms. NOT a toy, NOT a miniature or diorama or snow-globe, NOT smooth clay or plastic, NO tidy repeating wedding-cake tiers, NO cute rounded domes, no cartoon proportions, no flat even colour. Matte grimy materials, one low warm sun, deep shadows, strong rim light. NATURAL, NOT STAGED: nothing stands alone like a prop on a table; every structure is grown out of, carved into or half-buried in the rock, bases merged with scree, rubble and fallen blocks. Irregular organic outlines, uneven ground, off-centre and overlapping forms, no neat rows, no mirror symmetry, one obvious focal point. Ruins, NOT a city, no skyscrapers, no glass, no modern architecture, no green lush vegetation.

ENV-03.sheet: A single 3D-model reference turnaround sheet on a plain light-gray studio background: the same medium floating island of the same dark black-brown fractured boulder rock as the Starting Shelf Island, about 30 m wide, with a ragged uneven outline and a heavy rough underside. Along its north edge rises ONE GRAND MASSIF of natural rock: huge, thick and monumental, like a small mountain range or the great rock buttes of a canyon land, and like the tall rock clusters in the approved key art. It is a single mass that grows out of the island with no gaps at its base. It has a very wide heavy base about 22 m wide, and out of it rise five or six enormous crags of very different heights. TOWERING is the point. The crags are like the great spires of the Dolomites, the basalt pillars of Zhangjiajie and the fractured slate peaks of a mountain range, only crooked and leaning. THE BIGGEST CRAG RISES ABOUT TWICE AS HIGH AS THE WHOLE ISLAND IS WIDE (about 55 m on a 30 m island), so in the front view it is far taller than the island is long, and the island looks small beneath it. The second crag is about 38 m, then 34 m, 26 m, 18 m and 12 m, so the skyline is a jagged crown of very different heights: one extra tall spire, two or three tall ones, then medium ones and low broken shoulders. Do NOT make them all the same height. Every crag is thick at the base and rises in a long tapering shape, narrowing unevenly toward a ragged broken top, with long vertical fluting and deep vertical cracks, big ledges, overhangs and collapsed notches, wind grooves and thin lighter brown seams. They stand as ONE TIGHT OVERLAPPING CLUSTER, NOT in a fan, NOT in a row, NOT side by side like the fingers of a hand: some crags in front, some behind, two leaning against each other, one leaning out over the hollow, each leaning 10 to 25 degrees at a different angle, tops broken and jagged, the tallest off to the left of centre. They are fused at the base into one wide heavy mass with lower rock buttresses and stepped shoulders, with a few fallen boulders at the foot. They are NOT short blunt boulders, NOT squat blocks, NOT thin slabs, NOT planks, NOT fins, NOT ribs, NOT teeth, NOT stacked blocks, NOT toy bricks, NOT a neat row of equal stones, NOT like fingers, and NOT icicles or cones. In front of the crags the top dips into a small sheltered hollow with a plain flat floor of bare dark rock with nothing lying on it, thin straight bronze lines inlaid in the floor leading to one short stone column on a round bronze base with a small dark fire bowl on top, unlit. There are no steps, no stairs and no platforms. On the west edge a thin plank-and-chain bridge arrives at a short bronze socket post, and on the east edge a short fixed stone bridge end with a second short bronze socket post leaves toward the next place. At the south-east edge, away from the crags, a big flat-topped natural boulder with a worn smooth top sits right on the rim, facing the open sky. Nobody sits on it. ENV-04.sheet: A single 3D-model reference turnaround sheet on a plain light-gray studio background: the same large floating island of the same dark black-brown fractured boulder rock as the Starting Shelf Island, about 60 m wide, with sheer broken cliff faces all around, a ragged oval outline, and a deep underside like an upside-down mountain of fractured rock with a few long hanging rock tendrils and a faint bronze vein deep in the cracks. In the middle of the top is one DEEP CRATER, about 30 m across and 18 m deep, with sheer cracked rock walls and three broad broken ledges stepping down to a flat floor far below. The crater is an irregular oval, NOT round, NOT neat rings, NOT a stadium, NOT a quarry with tidy steps. Thin amber light glows faintly in the cracks of the crater floor and walls, dim and dormant, like a sleeping reservoir of energy. Thin straight bronze lines are inlaid in the crater floor.
